answer: In the nebula marketplace, each agent identity must lock a $100 bond for 30 days before it can bid for work. The bond acts as an economic anchor: creating names is cheap, but activating 10,000 of them ties up $1 million. Even a relic account must post the same bond. This does not prove identities are unique; it makes a swarm costly by forcing the attacker to finance every active identity for the full lock period.
